question: Should OpenClaw add a core child-visible pre-timeout warning/grace contract for sub-agent runs, and what public config or tool surface should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding it safely requires product choices about API naming, defaults, per-spawn overrides, and lifecycle behavior across native and ACP child runs.

options.title: Define Core Warning Contract
options.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, optionally with a carefully named per-spawn override, and cover native plus ACP warning delivery with lifecycle tests.

options.title: Focus On Post-Timeout Recovery
options.body: Decline child-visible pre-timeout warnings for now and invest in timeout notification, durable completion delivery, and resume/recovery behavior instead.

options.title: Document Prompt Checkpointing
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document operator prompting/checkpoint guidance without adding a new config or warning delivery mechanism.

recommendation.title: Define Core Warning Contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, optionally with a carefully named per-spawn override, and cover native plus ACP warning delivery with lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current review context and adjacent subagent lifecycle history for the product/API decision.
